title: ops-partner-36-day-slo-activation-experiment
content:
Executive summary:

This is a working note for a lightweight, time-boxed 36-day experiment to validate a friction-reduced SLO activation path for model-serving features that require cross-functional coordination. Goal: prove we can take a new SLO from proposal -> pilot -> initial enforcement with minimal handoffs and measurable improvement in incident-to-resolution time while maintaining developer velocity.

Why 36 days?
- Short enough to stay focused and iterate quickly.
- Long enough to collect signal across at least one full weekly cycle and an oncall rotation.
- Phases map to sprint cadence: 1 week discovery, 2 week pilot, 2 week rollout & stabilization, with a buffer week for retro and next-step decisions.

Scope (what we will include in the experiment):
- One model-serving route (chat-generate-v2) as the canonical test surface.
- Two SLO signals: P99 tail latency (30s window) and error-rate (5xx / client-visible failure) measured as a rolling 1h window.
- Error budget policy: soft alerts at 25% burn, mandatory review and page at 50% burn, rollback or canary pause at 90% burn.
- Cross-functional partners: SRE, Serving Runtime, Platform, Product (hosted-api), Observability and Solutions Eng.

Success criteria (quantitative + qualitative):
- Quantitative: reduce median P99 alert-to-ack time for this route by 30% compared to baseline across the pilot weeks. Reduce mean time to mitigations (first mitigation action) by 25%.
- Qualitative: partners report fewer coordination friction points; handoffs reduced to at most one required synchronous meeting per incident during pilot.

High-level timeline (36-day experiment):
- Day 0-7 Discovery and instrument: align on SLO definitions, metric names, dashboards, and alert thresholds. Create initial SLO proposal doc and confluence page.
- Day 8-21 Pilot: enable soft SLO alerting for chat-generate-v2 in staging -> shadow alerts in prod (no pages) then enable pages to oncall after "soft alert rehearsal" day. Run live drills.
- Day 22-35 Rollout & stabilization: enable enforcement policies (canary pause on heavy burn), validate rollback playbooks, and tune alert thresholds.
- Day 36 Retro & decision: collect metrics, retro notes, and decide next-step (widen to more routes, refine guardrails, productize runbook).

Roles and responsibilities (short RACI-style notes):
- Experiment lead (owner): Aisha Patel -> coordinate weekly syncs, keep decision log, slack channel moderator.
- SLO author and measurement owner: Jonah Kim (observability) -> ensure metrics name stability, define SLI queries, own dashboards.
- Runtime mitigations & feature flags: Ethan Brooks (serving-runtime) -> implement canary pause and quick safe-fallback variant.
- Platform enforcement & rollout: Marisol Ortega (platform-engineering) -> implement routing policy changes and capacity reservations for canary.
- Product & customer impact authority: Priya Nair (product-hosted-api) -> approves user-facing rollbacks and customer comms.
- Oncall liaison: Luca Rossi (sre) -> coordinates oncall drills and tracks incident timelines.

Tactical checklist (first 7 days):
- Draft precise SLO statements (owner +1): P99 latency < 1.2s for keys users; error rate < 0.5% 1h rolling. (TODO: confirm exact thresholds with product).
- Create observability queries (PromQL/Velociraptor) for P99, p95, mean latency, 5xx count, user-impacting errors. Tag metrics with route=chat-generate-v2, model_variant=redwood-v2.
- Build staging dashboard with traffic replay test harness.
- Add synthetic checker hitting the route every 30s to exercise tail latency.
- Draft alert rules: soft-alert (pager only to #slo-experiments), escalation to oncall at 50% burn, immediate page for >90% within 10m.
- Create the experiment channel: #ops-slo-36d-experiment (Slack).

Pilot playbook (days 8-21):
- Week 1 (shadowing): enable SLO measurement in prod, but send alerts to experiment channel without paging primary oncall. Capture false positives and tune.
- Week 2 (live paging): after tuning, route pages to oncall with runbook steps below. Conduct at least two planned drills during low-traffic windows.
- Runbook: initial triage -> check canary pause status -> switch traffic to fallback variant if applicable -> escalate to runtime owner if KV cache or batching anomalies detected -> notify product and CS if customer-visible degradation expected.

Runbook snippets (to include in confluence):
- Check telemetry: p99(latency, 1h), error-burst map, queue length, GPU host OOMs.
- Quick mitigations: toggle micro-batching to immediate, enable safe-fallback model at 10% traffic, increase timeout thresholds for downstream non-critical calls.
- Escalation: if no mitigation within 15m, pager to serving-runtime oncall and schedule 30m war-room.

Measurement plan and dashboards:
- Primary SLI queries included in the confluence page (owner Jonah). Use both event-based and sampling checks.
- Baseline collection: capture 14 days of historical data before enabling pages; store in /observability/archives/ops-slo-36d.
- Exported metrics for the experiment: alert-to-ack latency, ack-to-mitigation latency, mitigation-to-recovery, error-budget burn rate over time.

Risk register (open and evolving):
- Risk: noisy synthetic checks produce false burn. Mitigation: tune synthetic cadence and use weighted user traffic signals for burn calculation.
- Risk: canary pause causes user-visible regressions when fallback variant has lower quality. Mitigation: limit fallback weight and track quality evals alongside SLO metrics. Pre-approve customer-facing messages.
- Risk: operator fatigue from extra alerts. Mitigation: keep soft-alerts low-noise, keep clear demarcation between experiment alerts and production SLOs.

Open questions (notes to self / for reviewers):
- Do we want error-rate SLI to include client-side errors (4xx) for this route or only server-side 5xx? Recommendations due Day 2.
- Should we tie billing/quota reductions into error budget policy for this pilot? (Product decision).
- Is 1h rolling window appropriate for P99 burn sensitivity? Consider 30m for faster feedback.

Communications and cadence:
- Weekly 30m sync every Friday 10:00 PST (owner to share agenda + decision log).
- Daily async standup in #ops-slo-36d-experiment during pilot weeks (short bullets).
- Postmortem template to be used for any incident that causes >50% burn and lasting >1h.

Artifacts to deliver by Day 36:
- Final decision memo: adopt, abandon, or iterate (owner: Aisha).
- Cleaned dashboards and PromQL queries (owner: Jonah).
- Production-ready runbook and automated remediation playbooks (owner: Ethan + Marisol).
- Retro notes capturing friction points and proposed org changes to reduce cross-functional overhead (owner: Aisha + Luca).

Next immediate actions (today):
- Aisha: create confluence page and wire up experiment channel.
- Jonah: draft SLI queries and push initial dashboard to staging.
- Ethan: prototype canary pause toggle and simple fallback variant under feature-flag.
- Marisol: reserve capacity window for canary tests (low-traffic weekday) and add routing policy stub.
- Priya: confirm customer comms template and whether billing tie-ins are off-limits for experiment.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lightweight and reversible. The experiment is meant to capture where cross-team handoffs slow down SLO adoption and to validate minimal required automation to make SLOs actionable without slowing launches. Please add comments on the confluence page, and flag any blockers in the linked JIRA INF-2418 thread.

Appendix: useful links & references (local):
- Pre-read: "SLO primer for product folks" (confluence link on page).
- Past experiment inspiration: INF-runbook-pilot-2025 (internal).
- Observability playbook: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/docs/alerting-guidelines.md

Last edited by Aisha Patel on 2026-03-01.
